artifacts_produced.deploy_evidence: Owner key: MCPORTAL_OWNER_KEY_CLAIM (oid|sub) and MCPORTAL_OWNER_KEY, matched case-insensitively. An unset or other claim refuses with OWNER-CONFIG-MISSING. A header with neither oid nor sub refuses with HEADER-UNVERIFIED. Freshness: with iat present, the 120 s window applies; with no iat, the signed exp bounds the header on the injectable clock, and an expired header refuses with HEADER-STALE. MCPORTAL_CHANGES_TABLE is read first. There is one put_item per WRITTEN or REFUSED outcome, with ConditionExpression attribute_not_exists(pk). A record failure is reported as record=FAILED and never moves the verdict; lambda_handler prints the record state. MCPORTAL_OWNER_OID is no longer read.

New file with 6 named tests. It injects an ES256 test key, a fixed clock, a fake store and a fake changes client; the fake client traps UpdateItem, DeleteItem, BatchWriteItem and every other method. It uses no network and no AWS.
Unchanged and still green. handle() keeps its owner_oid= keyword as shorthand for owner_claim=oid. pytest over tests/: 10 passed, 4 of them existing and 6 new.

aws_dynamodb_table.mcportal_grant_changes is named mcportal-grant-changes-table. It is PAY_PER_REQUEST, with hash_key pk (S, PRINCIPAL#<tid>#<oid>), range_key sk (S, <UTC ISO ts>#<uuid4 hex>), PITR, SSE and deletion_protection. The writer role statement McportalGrantChangesPutOnly grants [dynamodb:PutItem]. The new aws_iam_role_policy.gw_read_mcportal_grant_changes (gateway-read-mcportal-grant-changes-policy, on aws_iam_role.gw) carries Sid GatewayReadsMcportalGrantChanges with [GetItem, Query, Scan]. Env: MCPORTAL_OWNER_KEY_CLAIM, MCPORTAL_OWNER_KEY and MCPORTAL_CHANGES_TABLE. var.mcportal_owner_oid is replaced by var.mcportal_owner_key_claim (validated oid|sub) and var.mcportal_owner_key, neither with a default. The naming gate passed 3 graded. terraform fmt -check rc=0. Nothing applied.
